Customs Act 2023: The Government has exercised its legal authority under various sections of the Customs Act 2023, specifically sections 263, 81, 90, 91, and the Second Schedule, to formulate and issue new rules.
National Board of Revenue: The Government is empowered to draft and issue rules under the Customs Act 2023 in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.

(৩) কাস্টমস আইন, ২০২৩ কার্যকর হইবার সঙ্গে সঙ্গে এই বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করা প্রয়োজন বিধায়, ইহা ৬ জুন, ২০২৪ তারিখে কার্যকর হইবে।

Goods Declaration, Assessment and Re-ass: These rules are formally titled as the Goods Declaration, Assessment and Re-assessment Rules 2024.
The rules apply to all import and export consignments.
The rules are effective from June 6, 2024, to coincide with the operationalization of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Act 2023: The implementation of the Goods Declaration, Assessment and Re-assessment Rules 2024 is contingent upon the enforcement of the Customs Act 2023.
The Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purposes of these rules.
Terms not explicitly defined in these rules shall carry the same meaning as attributed to them under the provisions of the Customs Act 2023.
Importer: The term importer is defined in accordance with the definition provided under the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Value: Customs value is defined as per the meaning assigned to it in the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Goods Declaration: Goods declaration is defined according to the meaning provided under the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Classification of Goods: The term H.S. Classification of goods refers to the definition established under the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: Appropriate officer of customs is defined in reference to the meaning provided under the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Exporter: The term exporter is defined according to the meaning provided under the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Duty and Taxes: Customs duty and taxes are defined in accordance with the meaning provided under the relevant section of the Customs Act 2023.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৩। পণ্য ঘোষণা ফরম।⎯ সকল প্রকার আমদানি ও রপ্তানি পণ্যচালানের জন্য পরিশিষ্ট-১ এ বর্ণিত পণ্য ঘোষণা ফরম আমদানিকারক বা রপ্তানিকারক বা তাহার নিয়োজিত এজেন্ট কর্তৃক সঠিকভাবে পূরণ করিয়া সকল প্রয়োজনীয় দলিলাদিসহ যথাযথ কর্মকর্তার নিকট দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

Goods Declaration Form: Importers, exporters, or their authorized agents must use the specific declaration form provided in the relevant appendix for all import and export shipments.
The declaration form must be accurately completed and submitted to the appropriate customs officer along with all necessary supporting documentation.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This official is designated as the authority to whom importers or exporters must submit their completed goods declaration forms and all required supporting documents for clearance.

Bill of Lading: This document is a mandatory requirement to be submitted along with the goods declaration during the import process.
Certificate of Origin: This document is a mandatory requirement to be submitted along with the goods declaration during the export process.
National Board of Revenue: The board, along with the government and other relevant departments, has the authority to issue orders from time to time specifying additional documentation requirements for both imports and exports.
Customs Invoice and Documentation: General invoices and packing lists are required for both import and export declarations, along with specific transport documents for imports and commercial contracts for exports.
Export: Exporters must provide specific supporting documents including sales contracts or letters of credit, invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin during the customs declaration process.

Customs Act 1969: The Act provides the legal framework for the assessment of goods and specifies the powers and duties of the appropriate officer of customs regarding the verification and determination of customs duty.
Customs Assessment: This process requires the submission of declarations and documentation by the importer, exporter, or their authorized agent according to specific rules.
The appropriate officer must ensure the validity of the declaration, perform classification, verify the country of origin, determine customs value, and calculate applicable duties and taxes.
The assessment process concludes with the issuance of an assessment notice, which must be communicated promptly to the importer, exporter, or their agent.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer is responsible for examining goods to confirm their importability, verifying submitted documentation, and checking the accuracy of the declaration against provided evidence.

The officer must adhere to the Act and relevant rules to conduct systematic verification, including assessment of classification and customs value, leading to the formal issuance of an assessment notice.
Goods Declaration: Goods declarations must be submitted by importers or exporters in accordance with established rules and within the prescribed timeframe.
The declaration is subject to thorough verification and validation against submitted documents and legal requirements to ensure its accuracy before customs duty is finalized.

Customs Act 1969: Section 90(3) of the Act serves as the legal foundation for implementing self-assessment procedures for specific categories of goods declarations.
Customs Assessment: Self-assessment is applicable for goods declarations filed by Authorized Economic Operators, low-risk goods identified through automated risk management, or specific entities authorized by the National Board of Revenue.
When performing self-assessment, required documentation must be submitted to the appropriate officer either directly or via the customs computerized system prior to final assessment.

If credible intelligence or complaints exist regarding a self-assessed declaration, or upon a voluntary request by the importer, exporter, or their agent, the appropriate officer must conduct the assessment process according to prescribed rules.
Authorized Economic Operator: Authorized Economic Operators utilizing the electronic green channel are eligible to utilize self-assessment procedures for their goods declarations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to designate specific persons or entities eligible for self-assessment through the issuance of official orders or notifications.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The customs computerized system serves as the primary electronic platform for submitting goods declarations and required documentation for the purpose of self-assessment.

৭। পুনঃশুল্কায়ন।⎯ (১) পণ্য ঘোষণার পুনঃশুল্কায়নের ফলে নূতন বা অতিরিক্ত শুল্ক, কর বা ফি পরিশোধের প্রয়োজন হইলে বা ভুলক্রমে ফেরত প্রদান করা হইলে এইরূপ শুল্ক, কর বা ফি পুনরায় আদায়ের লক্ষ্যে পুনঃশুল্কায়নের কারণ লিপিবদ্ধ করিয়া আইনের ধারা ৯১ এর উপ-ধারা (৩) অনুযায়ী পরিশিষ্ট-২ মোতাবেক সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিকে অবহিত করিতে হইবে এবং উক্ত পত্রে উল্লিখিত সময়ের মধ্যে লিখিতভাবে মতামত প্রকাশ ও শুনানির সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে হইবে।
(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এ উল্লিখিত সময়ের পর পুনঃশুল্কায়ন চূড়ান্ত করিতে হইবে এবং পরিশিষ্ট-৩ মোতাবেক দাবিনামা জারি করিতে হইবে।

Reassessment: This clause outlines the procedural requirements for the reassessment of goods, specifically when such reassessment necessitates the recovery of new or additional duties, taxes, or fees, or when refunds were granted in error.

The process requires documenting the grounds for reassessment and providing the concerned individual with formal notice according to the prescribed appendix, alongside an opportunity to respond in writing and attend a hearing within a specified timeframe.
Upon the expiration of the notice period, the reassessment must be finalized, and a formal demand notice must be issued according to the specified appendix.
Customs Act 1969: The reassessment process must be conducted in compliance with the requirements set forth in sub-section (3) of section 91 of the Customs Act 1969.

Goods Declaration Form: This document refers to the standard form used for the mandatory declaration of goods as required under the relevant customs rules.

Customs Act 2023: Section 91(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the customs authorities to review import or export declarations to ensure the accuracy of the assessed duties and taxes.
Section 91(3) of this Act serves as the legal basis for issuing a demand notice for the recovery of unpaid customs duties, taxes, and other applicable charges.
Business Identification Number: The Business Identification Number is required to be provided by the importer or exporter for the identification of the party involved in the customs declaration and clearance process.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: The Assistant Commissioner of Customs is the authority responsible for issuing the demand notice for the recovery of short-paid customs duties and taxes to the importer or exporter.
